📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel’s Wolverine may have started strong in September’s Circana sales report, but it plunged in October.

Sony’s big PS5 exclusive for 2026, which attracted reasonable if utterly unremarkable reviews, ranked 14th in the latest US best-sellers list – dropping dramatically from first position the month of its release.

Sources indicate that the game is now 15th overall for 2026 as a whole, down from 11th position in September. It’ll continue to fall with juggernauts like GTA 6 now officially out.

The exclusive’s lore accurate lack of legs can likely be attributed to the game’s worse than expected reviews.

While it’s not universally disliked – we awarded it an 8/10, after all – fans understandably expect better from dev Insomniac.

Sony’s running discounts on the game during Black Friday to try and stimulate some enthusiasm around it, and I suspect this may be one of those titles that ends up in a lot of hardware bundles in the future.

To be fair, the platform holder seemed relatively satisfied with the title’s 2.4 million sales during its recent financial report.

I suppose it’s possible the launch numbers really did meet its expectations, but it may now be disappointed with the title’s long-term momentum – or lack thereof.

We’ll probably have to wait until its next investor upgrade before we get more information.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, to get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, but you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to do it that way.
  • The GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300.
  • In a recent development, by the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, to get into the Kingpin Bowling Alley safe in GTA 6, you can either obtain the safe code, which is far harder than it sounds, or you can blow it open, but you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to do it that way. To help you choose, I'll explain both methods of getting into the safe below, including how to get the GTA 6 bowling alley safe code. Whichever road you go down, it'll help you save up some cash and get back on your feet - and take down a few of those pesky Kolt gang members while you're at it.

The GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is 0300. To find it for yourself, you need to go to Brooks Boatworks, as hinted at in the notepad next to the safe. The safe code is on a map on the wall in one of the buildings there, as marked on the image above.

In a recent development, by the time the bowling alley is mentioned, Brooks Boatworks should be marked on your map as another location held by the Kolt crew, and you may have even raided it already. Whether you've been there or not, the map is found on the wall of an office in the raised buildings to the east of the area, and you can find two other GTA 6 safe codes on this map, too.

Industry observers note that you'll have to fend off a lot of Kolt members at both the bowling alley and the boatworks, so make sure you've got some decent GTA 6 guns to hand, and certainly as much Zombix as you can carry. You'll find more at each location, too, so keep an eye out.

Industry observers note that you'll also see the option to plant explosives on the GTA 6 bowling alley safe, but if you haven't got the right explosives to hand, the option is grayed out. Unfortunately, this option requires reaching the Credit Check mission in Chapter 3, at which point you unlock the ability to buy sticky bombs from Ammu-Nation. Check out the full GTA 6 mission list to see how long you have to go.

Your best bet, therefore, is to open the GTA 6 bowling alley safe using the code, and at least you can even do that without ever entering the boatworks, thanks to us.

#63234. Latest Update: Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

Latest Update: Is it time to retire Dragon Quest as a series? Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it might be

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (431 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death.
  • Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something newly introduced.
  • In a recent development, "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something newly introduced. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

In a recent development, "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," said Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly fresh no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)".

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the fresh mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

Industry observers note that "What's key is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people.".

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the company aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

GTA 5's Steam concurrents have gone up rather than down now that GTA 6 is out, suggesting a lot of PC players are waiting

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week.
  • You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month.
  • According to recent reports, in fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the newly introduced one over.

You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB shows a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game.

According to recent reports, in fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. That's the beauty of PC gaming for you: Steam sales and mods keep games like this chugging along years after they'd be considered cutting edge.

GTA 5 holdouts might have a long road ahead of them though. GamesBeat reported last month that "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" said GTA 6 will make its way to PC in the first three months of 2027. In the past, Rockstar held PC releases back for at least seven months (GTA 5 PC took a year and six months), so an early 2027 release would be unorthodox if the report is true.

It has been revealed that GTA Online, or some kind of multiplayer mode, will hopefully come at some point and it would make some sense to drop it at the same time as a PC release, or at least that's what I tell myself at night. I've only played a few hours of the game and I'm already imagining the kinds of mods that will inevitably show up in the first week. Someone is going to make it so Jason can instantly gulp down his coffee for the stamina buff, I know it.

For now, PC players will just have to continue biding their time in GTA 5 and pray that Rockstar at the very least reveals a GTA 6 PC release date sooner rather than later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, publisher PLAYISM and developer viv have declared Saihate Station: Twilight Edition, a Switch version of the 2D exploration horror adventure game including the base game and downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” as well as two mini-games. It will launch on March 25, 2027 worldwide with English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese language support. A physical edition will be available in Japan for 8,800 yen.

Saihate Station first released for PC via Steam on March 7, 2025. The downloadable content “Twilight Railway” launched on April 18, 2025.

Here is an overview of the game, via PLAYISM:.

Since its release in March 2025, this 2D exploration horror adventure game has recorded a cumulative series total of 1.6 million downloads, an exceptional achievement for an indie free game, and continues to receive passionate support from fans in Japan and abroad. Now it is finally coming to Nintendo Switch!

Saihate Station: Twilight Edition includes the main game, the downloadable content “Twilight Railway,” and two mini-games, all in one package.

“After falling asleep on the last train, I woke up in a bizarre place called Saihate Station…”.

Haru Akinashi is a self-effacing office worker who lacks confidence and fails at everything he tries. Having slept through his stop on the last train, he finds himself trapped in a bizarre place called Saihate Station, where gruesome supernatural phenomena occur.

Shion Tatsunami is his complete opposite: a cheerful, talented colleague and former friend—happens to be there as well, and the two promise to work together to return home.

Their interactions are awkward at first, given the estrangement, but with each problem they overcome together, Haru recalls their former friendship, and their bond grows stronger than before.

Then, the truth of the world closes in.

It has been revealed that the main game features four multiple-ending story routes. The ending branches based on fluctuations in Haru’s “dependency level,” which changes according to the player’s actions.

Industry observers note that starting November 20, pre-orders for the physical edition will begin sequentially at retailers in Japan. As a first-print bonus, a “shaka-shaka acrylic stand keychain” featuring a train and character motif will be included. A limited edition featuring a special box with an “exclusive newly drawn mini-game book” and a “Haru-Shion handkerchief” is also planned. Bonuses and limited editions are available in limited quantities, so please place your pre-order early.

Call of Duty might have swapped guns and tanks for knights and swords if an Infinity Ward experiment had panned out

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold newly introduced directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day.
  • It has been revealed that this latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold newly introduced directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

It has been revealed that this latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty.".

According to recent reports, this isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

As for Kurosaki, he right now leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

This is thanks to a glitch that occurs when you change a specific setting and then spam the "View" button (formerly known as the "Back" button) on Xbox to trick the game into forcing you into first-person mode.

Here's how you do it (at your own risk - this is not an intended feature!):.

The same instructions apply if you're on PS5, but it's the touchpad rather than the View button.

It has been revealed that I've only been messing with this glitch a little bit so far, but it's pretty insane at first glance. You can run around, drive vehicles... do whatever you want to do. The only problem is that you can't actually back out of first-person once you're in it, although it seems some situations (like being arrested or going into a hair salon) will force you back into third-person.

According to recent reports, so, why is Rockstar hiding this feature from us? It's probably because it's still in a work-in-progress, and there are some items that don't seem to function properly with the first-person viewpoint yet. This does seem to indicate a first-person perspective is in the works though, similar to how it was added into GTA 5 later down the line.

I'll leave you with some very, very quick screengrabs of my own down below, along with a helpful video that's getting a ton of traction on YouTube explaining how to make it work.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • I don't know how you follow a $1.8 billion trip through Greek mythology, but Steven Spielberg apparently has an idea.
  • It has been revealed that the moment came Tuesday, Nov.
  • The only other thing I want to say, not to challenge you or anything, but there’s always The Iliad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I don't know how you follow a $1.8 billion trip through Greek mythology, but Steven Spielberg apparently has an idea. Christopher Nolan is still taking a victory lap for The Odyssey, one of the biggest hits on the 2026 movie schedule, and the Jaws director just floated a follow-up I'd pay good money to see. The way he brought it up made me laugh, too. Even Hollywood legends know how to suggest another movie without sounding too pushy.

It has been revealed that the moment came Tuesday, Nov. 17, at an awards-season screening of The Odyssey in Los Angeles. Spielberg moderated a Q&A with Nolan at the Directors Guild of America theater, where he praised the filmmaker's latest blockbuster before slipping in one more suggestion. As Gizmodo's Germain Lussier reported from the event, Spielberg told him:.

The only other thing I want to say, not to challenge you or anything, but there’s always The Iliad.

I love how politely Spielberg slid that into the conversation. It's the cinematic equivalent of complimenting somebody's enormous Thanksgiving dinner and then asking what they're making next year. He even followed it up by insisting there was no pressure. Nolan, understandably, joked that Spielberg seemed to be speaking for Universal Pictures. Spielberg admitted the studio would probably appreciate it, but he was interested himself.

Recent findings suggest that the idea makes a lot of sense. Homer's The Iliad takes place during the Trojan War, before Odysseus spends years trying to get home in The Odyssey. It wouldn't be a straightforward sequel, since we'd be going backward in the timeline, but the stories share a world. Imagine Nolan using his massive practical sets and IMAX cameras to tackle the conflict between Achilles and Hector. I'm already looking for a seat.

Here's what really makes the suggestion fun: Nolan almost got his shot at The Iliad decades ago. He was originally hired to direct Troy, the 2004 movie that eventually went to Wolfgang Petersen and starred Brad Pitt as Achilles. Nolan has since explained that he carried ideas from that unrealized project into The Odyssey, including the impressive Trojan Horse sequence.

Nolan has already explained why he chose The Odyssey. He considers The Iliad more grounded, while the later poem's monsters and stranger adventures offered something he hadn't seen done the way he envisioned. That doesn't mean he couldn't change his mind, especially after his latest movie has reportedly earned more than $1.8 billion worldwide.

Recent findings suggest that there's also something delightful about Spielberg being the person to make this pitch. He helped develop Interstellar before Nolan took over, and Nolan consulted him while preparing Dunkirk. Watching Spielberg praise Nolan as a fellow filmmaker and then immediately ask for another movie feels like the most recognizable fan behavior imaginable.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Recent findings suggest that for now, Nolan hasn't confirmed his next directing project. He told the crowd that he tends to focus on one film at a time and figures out the next one only after he's finished. So nobody should start booking tickets for The Iliad just yet. But if the man who gave us Jaws, Raiders of the Lost Ark, and Jurassic Park is personally asking for another giant Homer adaptation, I think somebody at Universal should at least write that suggestion down. Maybe keep the IMAX cameras handy.

In the meantime, The Odyssey is now available to rent or buy digitally, as well as on Blu-ray and 4K Blu-ray.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, smileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop.
  • SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing people to code their own simple programs and games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, smileBasic 4, one of the key pieces of software being used to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, is back on the Nintendo eShop. While the console's firmware has long since been updated to stop known jailbreak exploits, SmileBasic 4 itself has now also been patched.

SmileBasic is a line of programming tools which developer SmileBoom has released for various Nintendo platforms, allowing people to code their own simple programs and games. It's also opened multiple backdoors for jailbreak exploits over the years, first on 3DS, and then on Switch 2.

Technically, SmileBasic 4 is a Switch 1 game, but AI-backed hackers found a way to use it in order to jailbreak Switch 2 consoles, allowing the machines to run code not approved by Nintendo. That would allow customers to, in theory, run homebrew applications, but as far as I can tell, the exploit had not yet been extended to allow people to play pirated games.

It has been revealed that nonetheless, Nintendo acted quickly to delist SmileBasic 4 from the eShop and to patch the console's firmware to address the exploit at a system level. That's a necessary step, too, as SmileBasic 4 was not the only application that could be used to exploit it. Notably, Civilization 7, a game that is available on cartridge and thus impervious to delistings and software updates, could also be used for the jailbreak.

According to recent reports, even so, it seems that SmileBasic 4 itself has been updated to ensure that a similar exploit never happens again. As Twitter user MarioMasta64 notes, the software itself has gotten a upcoming enhancement post-reinstatement aimed at closing the hole used for the jailbreak. The application's demo – which could also be used to exploit it – has also been updated, but it has not yet been relisted on the eShop.

PS5 jailbreak dev indicates "just buy" GTA 6, because "things aren't looking good" for a game dump: "Don't say I didn't warn you".

According to recent reports, I know it, you know it, hell, I'm sure developer Archetype Entertainment know it: Exodus is kind of just Mass Effect again. That's in part because the DNA of the game has been built by series vets like Drew Karpyshyn, Chad Robertson and James Ohlen. But it's also because, well, they're putting FemShep in the game. Yes, I'm being a tad facetious here, but when the latest trailer for your game is literally titled "Female Jun Reveal," well, comparisons will be made!

Industry observers note that to top it all off, a blog post from the devs literally refers to the alternate gender for the protag as FemJun. They know what they're doing. In any case, first up, her voice actor! She's being played by Carina Conti, an up and comer last digitally heard in Mafia: The Old Country as Isabella Torrisi. Male Jun (who hasn't been given a nickname, which couldn't possibly serve to other female Jun (and MascJun is right there!)) has also had his voice actor confirmed as Stephen Oyoung, who you'll have heard as Mister Negative in Insomniac's Spider-Man games and Red Hood in Gotham Knights.

It's been previously confirmed that no matter which gender you pick for Jun, you'll be able to romance whoever you like, so, happy smoochin'! The story will stay the same too, as will dialogue options, though I'm imagine some pronoun switcheroos will take place somewhere along the line.

I'm mostly just left feeling that this doesn't really seem like it'll fix the game's boring hero problem. Edwin made note of Jun's quite lacklustre vibe earlier this year, aptly tearing down MascJun's Instagram visage, though this was prior to the face model and voice actor change the character has undergone. Personally, I'm not sure that'll be enough, and FemJun kind of matches that Instagram look; the perfect bun and bangs that pop out when she takes her helmet off is quite silly too. Ah well! A game isn't done until it's done (which, in theory, will be April 7th next year).

Queen's Domain has, by my count, four categories of collectible you have to hoover up if you want to see its more hidden endings, and some of them are real bastards to find⁠—I'd resigned myself to queueing up guides on YouTube to get it all done.

Sources indicate that guides are great, you might still need them for some of the collectibles, and if there's one game that feels like it was designed with Google/Reddit/forum help in mind, it's Queen's Domain. But I was thrilled to discover that, very late in the game, Queen's Domain provides a waypoint tool to guide you to its hidden collectibles. It turned what I worried would be a tedious process into yet another example of this game's boundless capacity for surprise and discovery.

I know I would have appreciated the heads-up, the permission to not worry about finding them all earlier in my playtime. If that's how you felt, and you aren't looking for spoilers, great: You can stop reading here. Granted, the spoilers in Queen's Domain are so absurd and out there as to be incomprehensible to someone early on in a playthrough.

According to recent reports, there are two requirements to get homing compass guidance in Queen's Domain: You need a fully kitted-out Mask of Second Sight, and to discover the hidden Petrified Garden zone. You can technically reach the latter from very early in the game, but you won't be able to open the necessary path until you acquire all of the lenses for the mask. Here's a quick checklist:.

That's basically, like, the entire third act of the game and encompasses most of the requirements for Queen's Domain's second of four endings⁠—this is super lategame stuff.

Recent findings suggest that you can reach the Petrified Garden by jumping off the teleporter platform while you're in the spacey void warping between zones. The large platform to the side you can dash to is a boss arena⁠—kill the familiar-looking guy here to reawaken the very high-level enemies in the garden.

Recent findings suggest that from there, you can find four god seals scattered through the zone with the Mask of Second Sight. Breaking them all opens a trap door to a secret area below the garden. At the end of the path, you can talk to a mysterious entity behind a sealed gate who spells out the criteria for unlocking endings three and four: Finding all mementos and silver-etched skulls in the game.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Industry observers note that they'll also, helpfully, provide a final duck to unlock fresh items at Umbada's shop. Among this last tranche of material, Umbada will now sell six charms that attach to the Mask of Second Sight. These charms reveal the locations of silver skulls, unopened treasure chests, treasure lizards, Gagi meals, data modules, and Orbewa eggs.

The respective tchotchkes appear as little holographic waypoints onscreen when you're within a few dozen meters of them and wearing the Mask of Second Sight. It can still take some sleuthing to reach the general proximity for these waypoints to appear, and there were some tricky placements that required me to think things through or circumnavigate the level and approach the waypoint from a different direction. But generally, the mask charms changed this collectathon portion of Queen's Domain into another fun part of the experience, rather than a completionist chore.

Breaking: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 is the US' best-selling physical game so far this year

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record.
  • The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November).
  • While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

The remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

While Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

Experience a young adult tale, set in the vibrant and bustling 1980s, that follows an innocent young man and two young “witches.”.

Sources indicate that three stars in parallel orbit, fated never to meet. The story of how these three completely different characters come to live under one roof will soon be revealed….

  • If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep.
  • Recent findings suggest that is the nickname FemJun too blatant?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

Recent findings suggest that is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

It has been revealed that there are, however, significant and key differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

In a recent development, archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons manufacturer Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Industry observers note that female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Recent findings suggest that archetype announced a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

It has been revealed that matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year.".

Xbox is handing out bans to GTA 6 players for uploading game captures that 'accidentally' breach its family and online safety guidelines.

On by default, game captures automatically uploaded to Xbox Live servers are scanned for offensive imagery, including hate speech, drugs misuse, excessive violence, as well as nudity and sexual content.

According to some Reddit sleuthing, GTA 6 players are being banned for uploading content captured on the beach in Leonida amongst other activities. The original poster claimed to have captured "zero nudity-just standard Vice City beach/coastal gameplay with NPCs in swimsuits/bikinis" before getting slapped with a ToS violation.

According to recent reports, if you think about it, it would be odd to walk around a beach with a video camera filming the locals, but it's a bit silly to see Xbox players getting 2-day bans. The rulings appear to be automated and unappealable too.

It's not clear if sexual content or nudity is the cause for the violation, but it's worth noting GTA 6 does contain full-frontal nudity. We'd recommend not spamming the capture button during those sequences. Xbox doesn't like that sort of thirsty behaviour.

Everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

Industry observers note that the world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (482 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness).
  • Sources indicate that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store.
  • "Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value consumers who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation users claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

Sources indicate that the case, brought by Alex Neill, who said she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value consumers who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

According to recent reports, the lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the company.

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game rolls out.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East Latest York.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

In a recent development, it's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox Newly introduced Zealand trick for eager players to try.

Breaking: GTA 6 has the best use of the PS5 controller I've ever seen

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (722 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing.
  • But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6.
  • GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me.

But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6.

GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. It's cool stuff.

Rockstar's smartest use of the triggers, and one of my favorite new features of GTA 6 in general, is its two-stage throttle for vehicles: When you pull the throttle (right trigger) in any car, there's a hard resistive stop at about the 50% to 60% point.

I've been calling this low-speed mode. At this speed, my car moves at a cruising pace that I find very comfortable—still slightly faster than NPC cars, but slow enough to follow the flow of traffic, take in my surroundings, or easily slam the brakes before running over a grandma on her way home from Canasta. I've also been calling it "normal driving" mode.

Don't worry, it's not hard to fully gun it either: Just pull the trigger with a little gusto and you're off to the races. This is what the two speeds look like:.

This has completely changed how I drive in GTA. I'm already someone who takes these games slowly, but the natural stopping point of the throttle makes this easy and natural—as if Rockstar is not just allowing for a more immersive playstyle, but endorsing it.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's just a different experience than having to manually learn the speed thresholds and intuitively hold the trigger at an exact middle point. This is more like I'm pulling the trigger to one natural stop for "slow", and another for "fast". It's the four-wheeled equivalent of Jason and Lucia's walk (you have to press L3 to enter a jog or sprint), or the default saunter of Red Dead Redemption 2's horses.

In a recent development, I can only recall one other open world game with a similar feature: the older Mafia games had speed limit toggles that automatically prevented cars from surpassing the speed limit. I always liked that, too, but this is more elegant.

It turns out Rockstar's co-branding campaign that insists GTA 6 "plays best on PS5" isn't just marketing. In these months before GTA 6 is a PC game, I really would suggest you play it on a PlayStation for the controller perks alone. And when the time comes, I hope Rockstar goes the extra mile to port these DualSense features to the PC version.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

Industry observers note that "What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely fresh modes, the possibilities are vast.".

It has been revealed that the post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

It has been revealed that anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a substantial visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one significant update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.
  • The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

The cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and stated the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

It has been revealed that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

According to recent reports, in September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of latest updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age update, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

"The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re playing GTA 6 and finding it too dark, there’s a good chance you may have your HDR calibration wrong – and no, it’s not your fault!

An extensive research video by HDTV Test – performed on a pricey Sony reference monitor – reveals the game’s HDR calibration may not be working quite as intended.

So while you may have followed the steps perfectly, setting your values until the Rockstar logo is only just visible as instructed, it may not be displaying optimally in your game.

I’d recommend you watch HDTV Test’s video for the full scientific analysis, but in short he explains that the various values in the HDR calibration settings output unexpectedly in-game.

Furthermore, the Rockstar release completely ignores Sony’s global PS5 HDR settings, so while you may have those calibrated perfectly for your particular screen, that won’t help you here.

Here’s how to fix it on PS5, according to HDTV Test – although do keep in mind your optimal personal settings will depend on your display, room, and preferred ambient lighting.

Load the game and press Options > Settings > Display > HDR Calibration.

HDTV Test recommends ignoring Rockstar’s own brightness calibration, so don’t worry too much if the manufacturer’s iconic logo is visible or not.

Instead focus on the two sample images of the party on the boat, which you can toggle between light and dark using R1.

These are the recommended starting settings for a display capable of 1,000 nits or higher:.

Feel free to tune these to taste; your own optimal HDR calibration settings will depend on your environment and screen, after all.

But this should help with the overall appearance of the game, and ensure you’re able to see a little bit better in the dark.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the launch of GTA 6, there was a whole lot of talk online about the Xbox "Fresh Zealand trick" and how people could get early access to the game by switching their regions to New Zealand on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.

We mentioned in various articles how it was a risky practice (against Xbox's ToCs), but one that had never traditionally resulted in any widespread bans, and it doesn't seem like either Xbox or Rockstar took any action at first glance.

As it turns out, a lot of people decided to give it a go for the new Grand Theft Auto.

This is according to the folks at Ampere Analysis (via The Game Business), who report that over 2.1 million people played GTA 6 in the US and the UK before it was officially released.

As you can see from the graph above, it seems the vast majority of those were based in the United States, followed by the UK, Canada, Brazil and Mexico. Only around 100,000 people tried the trick on PS5 in the U.S. (where it's harder to implement and requires a separate account), whereas 1.5 million of them ended up using it on Xbox.

Sources indicate that ultimately, the existence of the New Zealand trick probably led to a bunch of increased sales for Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, but it also poses the question of whether Xbox might be forced to put a stop to it on Project Helix and beyond. As much it's a beloved feature, it's also being used in a way that wasn't originally intended.

Let's see what happens in the future, but for now, it's clearly made a lot of people happy this week!

Did you use the New Zealand trick for GTA 6? Let us know your experiences with it in the comments.

  • If you hover your cursor over a fencing location icon on the GTA 6 map, you can see the rate each respective fence is offering for narcotics, marked bills, and jewelry.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that after the Clean Up After Donnie GTA 6 mission, Donnie becomes a fence you can sell narcotics, marked notes, and jewelry to, all you have to do is drop them in the deposit box at his trailer in Key Lento. But with Brian also a fence, you may be wondering whether it's more beneficial to sell your goods to Donnie or Brian. While one may offer more lucrative rewards, all that glitters isn't necessarily gold in GTA 6.

If you hover your cursor over a fencing location icon on the GTA 6 map, you can see the rate each respective fence is offering for narcotics, marked bills, and jewelry. In GTA 6 Chapter 1, Donnie (Donnie's Trailer) pays low for narcotics, and very low for jewelry and marked bills.

In a recent development, brian (Brian's Lockup), on the other hand, pays very low for all three types of illicit products. As such, Donnie pays more than Brian for narcotics. For example, if you collect all the cocaine drops Cal tells you about after the Clean Up After Donnie mission and fence them, Donnie offers you $3,400, while Brian offers just $2,720. Do note that the time it takes for these payments to reach your mailbox can be impacted by any available missions.

According to recent reports, while Donnie pays more, Cal suggests you sell the cocaine drops you collect to Brian, by depositing them at Brian's Lockup in Key Lento. He doesn't say why, but he seems to know something you don't. You should listen to Cal and sell your goods to Brian as the events of a later mission, called Swamped, might impact any payments Donnie owes you in GTA 6 (be aware of major spoilers by following that link).

Note that if you sell to Brian and he seems to be taking his time to pay you, there may be an available Brian mission you must complete before your payment is sent to the mailbox at Jason's House.

You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that word is out that Elon Musk has invested a significant amount of money in Skydance, making him part-owner of the newly merged studio alongside David Ellison. With headlines suggesting the organization may sell DC Studios and make other changes, I'm most concerned and have my eye on what the initiative is for Star Trek.

Recent findings suggest that it's been a tough year for Star Trek fans, despite it being the 60th anniversary. The year was marked by news that there are no latest shows on the horizon, and ended with the passing of Walter Koenig and, of course, the death of Patrick Stewart. As the year ends, I have mixed feelings about what the future holds and how these two men may impact it in 2027 and beyond. Let's talk about it.

Ellison had a history with Star Trek before becoming head of the studio that owns it. Skydance helped co-produce both Star Trek: Into Darkness and Beyond alongside Paramount when they were separate studios, and he was on the record as a card-carrying Trekkie.

Sources indicate that the CEO promptly mentioned Star Trek upon taking over Paramount in its original merger, and got the ball rolling on a newly introduced film. Unfortunately, we've seen this song and dance before with Paramount, as the issue was never developing a new Trek movie, but rather getting far enough along that it actually screens in theaters.

Additionally, Star Trek has zero reveals in active development at this time. With no fresh announcements about any progress on that front, it feels as though the game plan is to let the final seasons of Strange New Worlds and Starfleet Academy air in 2027, and then maybe announce a new direction for the franchise. That's just an optimistic guess, however, as we've gotten no confirmation that is the plan.

Which brings me to the main problem I've had with David Ellison thus far. He's stated that Star Trek has a significant role in what he wants to do with the future of Skydance, but we aren't really seeing any evidence of that. Right now, it feels like a lesser priority, something on the back burner, if you will, and I'm worried about just how long that will be the case.

In a recent development, elon Musk's entry into Star Trek puts another alleged Trekkie at the top of Skydance's ladder, which could propel moves into happening sooner rather than later. For those who don't know, Musk is actually a canon figure in the universe, having been directly mentioned by Gabriel Lorca as one of the great minds of humanity. Despite his various movie and film appearances, Musk has never appeared in Trek.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

As A Star Trek Fan I'm Eternally Grateful For What Patrick Stewart Did For The Franchise.

He's also preached about recreating Star Trek in real life via his SpaceX firm, but has simultaneously butted heads with other fans in interpreting what the series is about. We saw that when Starfleet Academy came out, and he openly joked about the show having obese actors and people wearing eyeglasses.

In a recent development, perhaps he was not privy to Gene Roddenberry's view that looks wouldn't matter in an idealized society. It doesn't seem to be the only message he missed, as Musk has openly criticized the franchise's embrace of diversity and inclusion, two major principles Roddenberry stressed from the beginning.

In a recent development, I feel as though Musk loves the part of Star Trek that is about space exploration, especially with it matching his eventual goal for humanity to expand and colonize other planets. It's imperative, however, for him to also understand the bit that the series is a morality play, and without that bit included, it ceases to be the franchise that's thrived for 60 years.

Industry observers note that now, it's entirely possible David Ellison and Elon Musk keep their hands out of Star Trek, and entrust someone else to do what they think will make it most successful. As it stands right now, I have my apprehensions about either being too hands-on with it, but maybe I'll be surprised a year from now.

Star Trek remains available to stream on Paramount+. I'm waiting for those final seasons of Starfleet Academy and Strange New Worlds, and hoping that movie goes into production by the end of next year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.
  • In a recent development, "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business.
  • Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ben Feder, the former Take-Two CEO who oversaw the launch of massive hits like Grand Theft Auto 4, Red Dead Redemption, Borderlands, and BioShock during his tenure, believes the resistance against gen-AI in games will vanish once the games industry has its 'Toy Story moment'.

In a recent development, "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," Feder told The Game Business. "People didn't think it looked good. Then Pixar released Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.".

Feder argued that the success of Toy Story ended the resistance against computer-generated animation, and the same could happen to games. Feder added, "My own view is that we are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI in video games in the West. In the East, they've already accepted it.".

Industry observers note that feder, who currently heads up venture capital fund Tirta Ventures, is investing in AI-first games. He, however, doesn't necessarily believe AI will reduce development costs, but that it also offers other advantages that could help game makers keep up with shifting consumer tastes.

In a recent development, "A lot of incumbents think about AI as a way of reducing costs, which it is," Feder said. "I query whether it will actually reduce costs, or will it just make games bigger for the same cost? But we're more interested in what AI can do to radically change gameplay.".

Recent findings suggest that feder views gen-AI simply as fresh technology that allows developers to do things they couldn't before. He likened it to Unreal Engine's instancing technology, which allowed Fortnite and other battle royale games to support 100+ players in a single server.

"That's question number one as we think about what we invest in: Was this possible before AI?" Feder said of his VC firm's strategy. "And when AI gets better, does the game get better? That's harder for an incumbent to focus on, because they deploy a lot of capital, have enormous advantages in terms of distribution, capital, and IP, and all of that needs to be protected.".

Sources indicate that there's been enormous pushback from players, developers and pundits against the use of gen-AI in games. Even so, more and more studios have revealed using some gen-AI during development, such as to assist with coding. More broadly, gen-AI adoption is on the rise across the industry, with a recent report estimating 40 percent of developers are using it.

Some development studios, such as Fortnite maker Epic Games, have doubled down on the use of gen-AI in game development. Epic is even more bullish on gen-AI in its Unreal Engine, which the company is at the moment transforming into an engine that's almost entirely driven by gen-AI and LLMs. Consumer sentiment remains sour, however, and the perception of the tool is not helped by the number of 'AI slop' games taking over Steam's storefront, the 'enshittification' of fan wikis, or the link AI seems to have to the unprecedented wave of layoffs that has shaken the industry over the past two years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few minutes into my first play session with Grand Theft Auto 6, I was doing my first bit of driving. I'd been cruising down the Leonida Keys, and as I was patiently waiting at a red light and humming along with the radio, I had a sudden realization: I was patiently waiting at a red light.

I immediately floored it, weaving into and out of oncoming traffic and channeling all the years of training in being a vehicular menace I'd been provided by prior Grands Theft Auto. But just a short way down the road, moments after blasting past a few panicked pedestrians I'd aggressively robbed of the right of way, it happened again: Without thinking, I'd come to a complete stop at a stop sign.I'm playing the world's most renowned automotive crime fantasy, and I can't stop observing the basic tenets of road safety.

Repeatedly across the hours I've put into GTA 6 since launch, I've been succumbing to an embarrassing habit of obeying driverly etiquette. I'm following other drivers at a reasonable distance when I could be forcing them off the road to save time. I'm diligently staying in my lane when I could be scraping my way up the shoulder at 90 miles an hour. NPC passengers have berated me mid-mission for not driving fast enough because I'm checking both directions before crossing an intersection. Something is wrong with me.

According to recent reports, to be entirely clear: I've never had this matter before. As with any other sensible person, my time in the two decades and change that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto have been characterized by a blatant disregard for roadway caution. If I was ever driving safely, it was either by accident or as a sort of affectation—like when you do a crappy posh accent to make fun of the moneyed classes.

But in GTA 6, something is different. Something has shifted in the simulation enough that I'm opting out of vehicular psychopathy without even meaning to—something in the increased visual fidelity and the intensified sense of heft and momentum. Something's stepped across some critical line of verisimilitude, and now I'm instinctively treating its virtual cars like the multi-ton slabs of explosion-propelled metal they're meant to evoke.

And it's not just the cars, either. There's a tweet circulating today from a Polish user who noted how firing a weapon in public feels more dire in GTA 6 than in previous entries, demonstrating the point with a video of panicked beachgoers fleeing en masse as Jason fires a pistol into the air. I can confirm that—perhaps not coincidentally—I've been doing a lot less non-vehicular psychopathy, too.

During in-mission firefights and gang raids, I'm as unphased by the violence on display as I've been by the collective years of videogame combat I've done beforehand. There, it's action movie absurdity. Elsewhere, though, I'm rarely reaching for a firearm. Age is partially to blame: Random acts of simulated violence aren't as titillating at 33 as they were at 12. But the truth is, Rockstar's absurd expenditure of art and animation tech has produced a crime game where firing a gun with no good reason can feel downright criminal.

Industry observers note that when there's so much attention dedicated to how characters move and shift their mass, when the world around them is lit so believably and packed with so much detail, the violence you can inflict feels so much more acute. I don't think it's immoral to shoot a gun or drive a car at someone in GTA 6. But I do think it feels queasy—queasy in a way I'm not used to feeling. The uncanny valley isn't newly introduced, but being able to empty a weapon into it is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a significant u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones remarked during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

According to recent reports, that last bit seems likely to have been noted with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

Industry observers note that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the organization navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board confirmed yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the firm’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is right now serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard.
  • Sources indicate that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the latest late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold.
  • It has been revealed that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Players who abused World of Warcraft: Forever's Blackmaw Hold unintended gold farm, which allowed a small minority of players to hoard thousands of gold in a few days, have drawn the ire of WoW publisher, Blizzard. Suspensions have been issued, trade locks have been put on accounts, and ill-gotten gold is being seized.

Sources indicate that for those unaware, the World of Warcraft: Forever community was greatly alarmed by this gold farm, which had players clear the same non-elite enemies from the latest late game dungeon, Blackmaw Hold. By quickly clearing select mobs with area-of-effect damage, players would loot upwards of 100 raw gold an hour. This exploit, clearly not intentional, was nonetheless farmed until Blizzard hotfixed it earlier in the week.

It has been revealed that there was much speculation on what would happen to those who participated in this exploit. That speculation would come to an end late last night with an official statement from the World of Warcraft: Forever development team.

According to recent reports, "As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced," the statement reads. "Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

According to recent reports, it goes on to explain the nature of the bug that made this gold farm possible, before reassuring those who may have accidentally benefited from some extra cash from their regular runs of Blackmaw Hold they have nothing to worry about. The same cannot be said for those who took advantage of the situation.

"Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug," it continues. "But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

It has been revealed that "Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.".

The post concludes by thanking players for their feedback on the matter, and a final warning: "As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.".

This decision certainly sets the precedent moving forward with World of Warcraft: Forever that such exploits won't be tolerated, and rolling back the wealth of those who made out of Blackmaw Hold like bandits is a good measure that should prevent continuous damage.

According to recent reports, inevitably the exploit would have had some impact, specifically in those days prior to trading blocks being put in place. While the gold on the exploiter's accounts may be removed, any purchases they made on the in-game auction house will have affected others through buying and selling goods with ample funds.

In a recent development, those who were suspended temporarily will be able to regain access to the game by the time the first wave of raids come out in December, so it very much feels like a firm slap on the wrist in that regard. Even so, given the establishment of punishments for such behavior, one can only wonder if future events will come with harsher penalties.

World of Warcraft: Forever, despite this small economic roadbump, is proving exceptionally popular for Blizzard. It's already broken records for the series, and has impressed players so far with its revamping of the classic MMO.
